options.E: Respirable crystalline silica released as rock is fragmented

edits.correct_answer: E. Respirable crystalline silica released as rock is fragmented
edits.why_correct: Crystalline silica from cutting, drilling or blasting stone, sand and granite causes silicosis, a pneumoconiosis with small upper-zone nodules and hilar nodes that may show eggshell calcification. Risk rises with cumulative dust exposure, and dust control and masks reduce it. People with silicosis also have an increased risk of tuberculosis and lung cancer. Source: UK Health and Safety Executive, Silicosis (hse.gov.uk/lung-disease/silicosis.htm); standard occupational respiratory teaching.

edits.stem:
A 69-year-old man has had 3 days of fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. A chest X-ray confirms right lower lobe consolidation. He is alert and orientated, with a temperature of 38.9°C, pulse 104/min, respiratory rate 22/min, blood pressure 128/76 mmHg and oxygen saturation 93% on air. His C-reactive protein is markedly raised. The admitting doctor calculates his CURB65 score.

Which of his findings contributes a point to the score?

options.A: His age of 69 years on presentation

edits.correct_answer: A. His age of 69 years on presentation
edits.why_correct: CURB65 gives one point each for new confusion, urea above 7 mmol/L, respiratory rate of 30 or more, low blood pressure (systolic under 90 or diastolic 60 or less) and age 65 or over. This man is alert, with a respiratory rate of 22 and normal blood pressure, so of the findings given only his age scores; his urea is not yet known. Fever, tachycardia, pleuritic pain and CRP are not part of the score, so clinical judgement and oxygen saturation must be used alongside it. Source: NICE NG250 Pneumonia: diagnosis and management, 2025 (Box 2, CURB65).
